: 5}\"}],\"structuredContent\":{\"sum\":5},\"isError\":false,\"_durationMs\":4}\n7:> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine
with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n13:`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connect
s your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses,
and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-ho
sted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n23:With results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only th
e credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, projec
t selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and wh
ether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run r
equest sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the mo
del, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no de

bit, quota draw, or balance refusal.
29:### 1. Write a suite
34:schemaVersion: "2"
37:suite:
46: model: anthropic/claude-ha

iku-4.5
53: steps:
58: kind: assert

60: type: toolCalledAtLeastOnce
64: steps:
6
9: kind: assert\n70: assertion:\n102:Change `toolName: read_note` to `toolName: echo` in the first case and run agai
n: the command exits `1` and names the failing assertion. Fix it, then rerun just that case and keep a report:\n114:1. `--server <
name>=<url>` (repeatable; HTTP(S) only). For a suite with exactly one target, `--url` / `--command` and their auth flags bind it i
nstead.\n119:Paths are relative to the directory you run the command in, not to the suite file. An explicit `--mcp-config` can bin
d some servers while the two conventional files still supply the rest. A lower-precedence file is read only while names remain unb
ound, and entries for servers the suite does not target are ignored — their processes are never started. Every name still unbound
is reported together (exit `4`).\n129:| `auto` (default) | `provider/model` and the provider's key is set | BYOK |\n130:| `auto` |
`provider/model`, no key | MCPJam, when it serves the model and you are signed in |\n131:| `auto` or `mcpjam` | `mcpjam/provider/
model` | MCPJam |\n133:| `byok` | `provider/model` | BYOK; the provider key is required |\n134:| `mcpjam` | `provider/model` | MCP
Jam; the model must be one MCPJam serves |\n144:`--host <template>` emulates one existing host template — its `initialize` identit
y, advertised capabilities, protocol versions and tool visibility, plus its model settings where the suite does not set them. It n
ever launches the real client, and reports say \"emulated\". The suite's model, and any authored `systemPrompt` / `temperature`, w
in over the template's. `target.hosts` in the file is recorded as declared but not executed, and `target.environment` as declared
but not resolved.\n148:A local suite file does **not** take a reasoning effort yet: `defaults` has no\n150:suite's default config,
which has not shipped), so the value is rejected as an\n151:unknown key rather than accepted and ignored. Ways to run a local sui
te at an\n155: model selection carries `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the runner applies it\n156: (and refuses a model that can
not) — see [`HostRunner`](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/host-runner#reasoningeffort).\n158:* Set the effort on the hosted
suite's model selection with\n163:A suite's `defaults.toolPolicy` is enforced before the MCP call: a denied tool never reaches the
server, the model receives the refusal, and the report records the block by case, iteration and call id. A blocked call is not gr
aded as a call and is not an executed tool span. A `deny` name that matches no tool the servers expose is invalid input (exit `2`)
; an unmatched `allow` is a warning. With no `toolPolicy`, nothing is restrained.\n167:> For the upcoming Inspector eval runner wi
th MCP App view tools enabled, use `view:<name>` in a suite's `toolPolicy.allow` or `deny`, for example `view:make_move`. These na
mes wait until the app renders; plain tool names keep the validation described above. Assertions and side-effect manifests still u
se `make_move`. This syntax does not enable view tools in the local SDK suite-file runner.\n185:| Prompt steps (including several
per case) | Run as one conversation per iteration |\n186:| Deterministic assertions (steps and `assertions`) | Graded with the hos
ted assertion engine |\n187:| Direct `toolCall` steps | Refused before anything runs — use a prompt, or run hosted |\n188:| `inter
act` steps, widget/render and tool-discovery assertions | Refused before anything runs |\n189:| Gating assertions on tool results
or per-call latency (`toolResultContains`, `toolResultMatches`, `toolResultMatchesSchema`, `toolResultSizeUnder`, `toolLatencyUnde
r`) | Refused before anything runs — a local run does not capture tool results or timings yet. An advisory one is reported as not
measured |\n192:| `suppressedSuiteStandardCheckIds` | Refused — a local run has no suite-standard registry |\n194:Every selected c
ase is checked before any model or tool call, so an unsupported later case costs nothing. Hosted-only capabilities run with `mcpja
m cloud eval run --file <file>`.\n198:* With `--format human` (the default on a terminal), a summary: the verdict, each case's gra
deable-iteration count against its threshold, failing assertions, not-measured iterations, policy blocks and un-run judges.\n203:E
very report identifies the run as local and emulated, carries the source-file sha256, the per-case evaluator hashes, the selection
, the effective model and rail per case and each server's binding source, and states that upload was off. Server headers, environm
ent objects, command lines and token-bearing URLs never appear in any output, and every credential the run was given is redacted w
herever observed text (an error, a tool argument) repeats it.\n205:The unit of a verdict is the **case**; iterations are evidence.
A JUnit consumer receives a `<failure>` only for a measured failure — provider errors, evaluator errors and interrupted work are
reported as skipped, never as failed assertions.\n214:| `3` | Missing or rejected model or platform credentials, including during
execution |\n222:The same engine is `runSuiteFile` in `@mcpjam/sdk`. It takes explicit bindings and credentials — it reads no file
s, environment or login store — and returns the decision and the report. See [runSuiteFile](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/
run-suite-file.md).\n", "exit_code": 0, "status": "completed"}}
